newsitem.title: USA: U.S. propane stocks fall by 2.2 mln bbls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. propane stocks fall by 2.2 mln bbls.

text.p: U.S. inventories of propane continued their expected seasonal decline last week, falling 2.2 million barrels to slightly below the normal range for this time of year, a government report showed Wednesday.
The Energy Information Administration report, however, said total U.S. stocks of this home heating fuel and chemical feedstock were still slightly above year-ago levels.
As of February 21, total U.S. stocks of propane were about 25.5 million barrels, about 3.8 million barrels above year-ago levels.
Much of the expected draw occurred in the key Gulf Coast hub, where stocks fell 1.9 million barrels in the week to 11.7 million, the EIA said.
In line with previous reports, the Midwest only dipped down, less than 100,000 barrels, as did the East Coast, a bit more than 100,000 barrels. The two hubs are significant home heating markets.
The EIA report said the recent pattern of modest draws in the two hubs amid sharp drops in the Gulf may indicate a strong demand by petrochemicals offsetting a weak demand for home heating.
